claims.text: Stabilizing ultrafine grain boundaries in an FCC/BCC HEA protective coating enhances its creep resistance.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing can produce an ultrafine-grained coating microstructure.
Controlled annealing after severe plastic deformation can make the ultrafine grain structure thermally stable.
Minor alloying additions may stabilize the ultrafine grain structure.
The engineered ultrafine grain boundaries resist coarsening during sustained loading.
Refined grain boundaries impede dislocation motion.
Refined, stabilized grain boundaries impede grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding reduce the steady-state creep rate.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding delay progressive plastic deformation under continuous load.
The modified coating will have a lower steady-state creep rate than the conventional-grain-size baseline.
The modified coating will accumulate less plastic deformation than the baseline.
The modified coating will exhibit minimal grain growth during creep testing.
The engineered grain boundaries will remain stable during creep testing.
The proposed creep-resistance effect is expected under sustained stress at temperatures below approximately 0.7 Tm.
The effect may become limited or variable at extreme temperatures or stresses.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in creep rate and accumulated plastic strain would refute the proposed enhancement.
Grain coarsening at a rate similar to the control would refute the proposed grain-boundary-stabilization mechanism.
